paragraphs: Markets over the last day: the eight tracked equity indices moved +0.69% on average, with Nikkei 225 strongest (+1.39%) and Nasdaq weakest (+0.08%). Brent crude changed +0.19% to 106.12. Gold changed +0.73% to 4,200.6001. Bitcoin changed -0.01% to 82,130.3594. The US 10-year yield stands at 5.089%, a relative move of -1.95%. Among the firms tracked, EQT (+4.40%) and BlackRock (+4.38%) moved the most.

Deals and capital markets: Credit Suisse bankers denied bonuses stripped after UBS takeover (FT World). Switzerland’s top court sides with government decision, overturning ruling of lower court Deals and capital markets: India approves biggest foreign takeover of domestic bank (FT Companies). Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings to buy nearly 61% of IDBI Bank for $5.6bn Central banks and macro: ‘Early days’ to see full effect of energy prices on inflation, BoE’s Bailey says (FT World). Lengthy period of higher costs would squeeze corporate margins and spur some companies to raise prices Central banks and macro: Rising inflation piles pressure on US voters ahead of midterm elections (FT World). Also in today’s newsletter, are Democrats developing an advantage among independent voters? Geopolitics and trade: How will Big Oil spend its $32bn Iran war windfall? (FT Markets). Investors are keen to see how the world’s largest crude companies plan to deploy extra cash generated by soaring energy prices
